title: Solo hobby dev: how would you improve the visuals of my browser poker game (SVG + CSS, no illustrator)?
author: joaocamu
selftext:
Hi everyone! I'm building \*\*All-in Aura\*\*, a Texas Hold'em game that runs in the browser. It's a No-Limit poker table with a twist, where players build up "aura" and spend it on abilities, pacts and territories that bend the rules, inspired on some anime power systems (mostly hunterxhunter and jujútsu kaisen). There are bot opponents with their own portraits and personalities, a masked dealer character called Ninefold, a tutorial and an online mode so friends can play together from their phones/browser. The chips are fake, and there's no money involved of any kind.  
  
I'm making it to play with my friends and family, so hiring an illustrator isn't in the plans right now. If they end up loving it, paying an artist to do a proper pass is something I'd consider down the road.  
  
How the visuals are made, right now:  
  
\- TypeScript + Vite, no UI framework  
\- Everything visual is \*\*SVG and CSS\*\*: the table, cards, chips, bot portraits and the dealer (layered SVG, generated by a small Python script)  
\- Animations use only CSS transforms and opacity, so it stays smooth on cheap phones  
\- A neon, dark "underground club" palette, with one color per aura type  
  
I've tried Gemini API for image generation. The results were interesting, but the cost ended up far above what I expected for a hobby project, so I stopped. A friend suggested using \*\*Figma's AI connected to Claude\*\* to generate and iterate on assets. I haven't tried it yet. Has anyone used that workflow? Is it worth it for game art? Could i run this on a small paid plan from figma?  
  
Screenshots are attached. I'd love any feedback, like:  
  
\- What looks off or amateurish at first glance?  
\- Cheap or free tools/workflows for someone who is comfortable with code and bad at drawing?  
\- Tips for making the portraits and the dealer feel more cohesive and less "clip art"  
\- Any layout or readability problems on the table screen  
  
Brutal honesty is welcome. Thanks for reading!  
  
Also, the game is online even tough is not finished yet. It’s on [https://allinaura.defixio.com.br](https://allinaura.defixio.com.br) (i will change the domain in the future, When i end trimming things up).
